questions.q: In Gane-Sarson DFD notation, which of these is NOT one of the four standard elements?
options: External entity
Process
Data store
Activation bar
questions.explain: The four DFD elements are external entity, process, data store, and data flow. An activation bar is a sequence-diagram element (Lesson 5), not a DFD element.

questions.q: Per this lesson's rule, what does it mean if a DFD seems to need a direct arrow from one data store straight to another?
options: That's a normal, valid pattern and should be drawn as-is
A process step is missing from the diagram — data should always move through a process, never directly store-to-store
It means the diagram should be converted into a sequence diagram instead
It means the two data stores should be merged into one
questions.explain: A DFD never connects two data stores (or two external entities) directly; data always moves through a process. A perceived need for a direct store-to-store arrow signals a missing process step, not an exception to the rule.

questions.q: What does 'leveling' let a documentation set do, per this lesson?
options: Encrypt sensitive data flows so only authorized readers can see them
Show the same process at increasing levels of detail — context, Level 0, Level 1 — so each audience can stop at the depth that answers their question
Automatically convert a DFD into Salesforce Flow metadata
Remove the need for a system context diagram entirely
questions.explain: Leveling starts with a single context-level bubble and explodes it into increasing sub-process detail across Level 0 and Level 1 diagrams, letting an executive stop at a high level while an implementer reads further.

questions.q: In the lead-routing Level 0 DFD example in this lesson, what role does the 'Territory data store' play when the 'Apply assignment rule' process reads from it?
options: It is the external entity that triggers the whole process
It is a data store the assignment-rule process reads from to make its routing decision
It is itself a process that transforms lead data
It represents the Sales Rep receiving the final assigned lead
questions.explain: The Territory data store holds territory data at rest; the 'Apply assignment rule' process reads from it (alongside the Lead data store) to decide how to route the lead — a data store is read from or written to by processes, not the other way around.

questions.q: What is the key difference between a data-flow diagram and a sequence diagram, as this lesson contrasts them?
options: A DFD shows timing and exact call order; a sequence diagram does not
There is no real difference — they are two names for the same diagram
A DFD shows how data moves between processes and stores without specifying timing or order; a sequence diagram's entire purpose is to show the exact order of calls in one transaction
A sequence diagram can only be used for Apex code, while a DFD can only be used for Flows
questions.explain: A DFD is deliberately silent on timing — two flows on the same diagram could happen seconds apart or overnight. A sequence diagram exists specifically to capture exact call order and timing within one transaction, which Lesson 5 covers.
